19838.title: Add per-table SHADOW enforcement mode for storage and query quotas
19838.author: Tarun-kishore
19838.summary: Add per-table quota enforcement modes. New optional QuotaConfig fields storageQuotaEnforcementMode and queryQuotaEnforcementMode (enum QuotaEnforcementMode: DISABLED|SHADOW|ENFORCED; null==ENFORCED, omitted from serialized form). SHADOW detects a breach, records the metric (QUERY_QUOTA_EXCEEDED broker meter / new STORAGE_QUOTA_EXCEEDED controller meter) + warning log, but does not reject the query / block offline push / pause realtime consumption. DISABLED skips the check. Storage effective mode is DISABLED if the controller-wide storage check is off. Hybrid table referenced w/o type suffix: strictest configured mode among existing OFFLINE/REALTIME wins. Added in 1.7.0 (master==1.7.0-SNAPSHOT). Documented 2 rows in reference/configuration-reference/table.md#quota and a new Enforcement mode subsection in build-with-pinot/querying-and-sql/query-execution-controls/query-quotas.md.

20097.title: Avoid repeated force commits during rebalance
20097.author: Jackie-Jiang
20097.reason: Internal controller rebalance correctness/performance fix (labels: bug, ingestion, performance, real-time, segment-rebalance; fixes #20095). The fix tracks already force-committed partition group IDs in an IntOpenHashSet for the whole rebalance so each partition's consuming segments are force-committed at most once; successors created by an earlier force commit are no longer re-committed on IdealState version-race retries or later movement steps (removes the old 'shouldForceCommit = false' one-shot-per-outer-iteration flag in favor of per-partition dedup). No new config key, default, query option, SQL function, public API signature, table-config field, or wire/serialization format. The existing rebalance 'forceCommit' option (documented in operate-pinot/rebalance/rebalance-servers/README.md: 'Whether to force commit consuming segments for a REALTIME table before they are rebalanced', default false) keeps the same meaning and default; the summary fields (isForceCommittingConsumingSegments, totalSegmentsForceCommitted) are unchanged. The PR notes an internal trade-off (fewer forced rollovers vs. potentially more stream replay in later steps), but that is a refinement of a double-commit bug, not a documented contract, so no docs page becomes stale and nothing new needs documenting. Not docs-relevant.
